---
# Quarto slide headmatter — https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/
# Copied to the course root as slides_headmatter.qmd by /course-maker course init
# (when the course's slide format is quarto). This is the course-level config;
# the per-lecture title fields are filled in when the first chunk of a lecture's
# slides.qmd is generated. Edit themes, fonts, and format options here.
#
# The title slide is generated from the four fields below — do not write a `##`
# heading for it. Slide 1 is this title slide, slide 2 is the outline.
title: "[Lecture] N. [Title]"
subtitle: "[Course name]"
author: "[Author]"
institute: "[Institution]"
lang: en
# ^ course language as a BCP 47 tag; drives hyphenation and generated labels.

# Three render targets from one source. The export command always names one
# (`quarto render slides.qmd --to revealjs|beamer|pptx`); a bare `quarto render`
# would build all three.
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: default
    # theme accepts a built-in name, a custom .scss, or a list of both.
    slide-number: c/t
    incremental: false
    embed-resources: false
    # embed-resources: true produces a single self-contained .html (larger file,
    # no sidecar directory) — useful for handing the deck to students.
  beamer:
    aspectratio: 169
    pdf-engine: xelatex
    # REQUIRED for any course not written in the Latin alphabet:
    #     mainfont: "DejaVu Serif"
    # xelatex reads Unicode source happily, but with no mainfont it typesets in
    # Latin Modern, which has no Cyrillic/Greek/CJK glyphs. The PDF then builds
    # WITHOUT ERROR and simply has no text where those characters were. Nothing
    # warns you. This affects the beamer target only — revealjs and pptx are
    # fine either way.
    # Pick a font that covers the script and exists on this machine:
    #     fc-list :lang=ru family        # substitute the course's language code
    # DejaVu Serif is a good default where available: it ships with TeX Live and
    # covers Latin, Cyrillic, and Greek. `course init` fills this in for a
    # non-Latin course; set it by hand if you change the course language later.
    # theme: Madrid     # any Beamer theme installed in your TeX distribution
    # colortheme: seahorse
    #
    # Speaker notes injected by /course-maker notes N reach Beamer as \note{}.
    # They are not shown unless you ask for the two-screen layout. Quarto
    # already loads pgfpages, so this one line is all that is needed:
    # include-in-header:
    #   text: |
    #     \setbeameroption{show notes on second screen=right}
  # To use your institution's template deck, replace `pptx: default` with:
  #   pptx:
  #     reference-doc: template.pptx
  # The template must define the layouts Quarto writes into: Title Slide,
  # Title and Content, Section Header, Two Content, Comparison,
  # Content with Caption, Blank.
  # A format key with only comments under it parses as null and fails the
  # render for every target — keep a value here.
  pptx: default

execute:
  echo: false
  # Figure chunks are illustrations, not content — the plot is shown, the code
  # is not. Override per chunk with `#| echo: true` when the code IS the point.
  # cache: true
  # ^ uncomment when a chunk is expensive (plots from a trained model). Results
  #   are reused until the chunk changes; force recomputation with
  #   `quarto render slides.qmd --cache-refresh`.
---
